STATE CAPTURE INQUIRY

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
We look at President's round about turn to agree to institute a commission of inquiry into State Capture 14 months after the Public Protector's State Capture report and numerous legal challenges.

We ask why now and what is the road ahead.

Further information:
it’s the story of one shocking revelation after another, from the Guptas’ private use of Waterkloof Military base for their 200 wedding guests to their infamous R600 million attempt to bribe Mcebisi Jonas to take the job of Finance Minister. Over a year ago, former Public Protector Thuli Madonsela released her damning State of Capture Report, implicating the Gupta brothers, as well as their close friends President Jacob Zuma, his son Duduzane and other senior state officials, in the gross misappropriation of public funds. Now, the President has finally appointed Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo to head up the inquiry Madonsela recommended. As civil society organisations and political parties welcome Zuma’s decision, Carte Blanche analyses the impact of the State Capture Commission Inquiry.

Press Release:


The State Capture Inquiry
State Capture: it’s the story of one shocking revelation after another, from the Guptas’ private use of Waterkloof
Military base for their 200 wedding guests to their infamous R600-million attempt to bribe Mcebisi Jonas to take the
job of Finance Minister. Over a year ago, former Public Protector Thuli Madonsela released her damning State of
Capture Report, implicating the Gupta brothers, as well as their close friends President Jacob Zuma, his son
Duduzane and other senior State officials, in the gross misappropriation of public funds. Now, the President has
finally appointed Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo to head up the inquiry Madonsela recommended. As civil
society organisations and political parties welcome Zuma’s decision, Carte Blanche analyses the impact of the State
Capture Commission Inquiry.

Script:


STRUCTURE STATE CAPTURE – 7 MINUTES (2.5 / 3 pages)

VO: The stage was set for the ANC’s newly elected National Executive Committee’s first meeting, in the Eastern Cape this week. With rumblings of President Zuma’s recall growing louder by the day.

LINK: But on the eve of the NEC meeting, President Jacob Zuma threw a curve ball – he announced the appointment of a commission of inquiry into State Capture - in line with the original recommendations made in the Public Protector’s Report

VO: Although the decision has been welcomed, Ben Theron from civil action organisation, OUTA, is sceptical about the sudden move.

BEN: PResident Zuma is a strategist at heart – he has been able to out play =- be one step ahead // what we believe he has done is another chess move //INT2 M1

VO: Political Analyst Ralph Mathekga agrees the move was calculated.

RALPH: I think his intention was to soften the blow with the NEC – because one of the core demands for he needs to go is his reluctance to deal with state capture INT1 M7

VO: The State of Capture report, that was released 14 months ago, called for a commission of inquiry that should be lead by a judge - selected by Chief Justice Moegeng Moegeng, and NOT the President, as he has been implicated in the allegations centred around corruption linked to the Gupta Family.

President Zuma delayed the process by legally challenging the validity of the report’s remedial action, arguing that it is unconstitutional and it infringes on the State’s separation of powers.

LINK: But when the constitution was drafted no provision was made when a President would have to commission an inquiry into himself – taking us into unchartered terrority.

VO: In December, a ruling was made in the North Gauteng High Court. Judge President Dunstan Mlambo found that the Public Protector does have the power to instruct the president to exercise executive authority. This means the remedial action was lawful.

President Zuma announced he would appeal the ruling, but then just three weeks later - he conceded - albeit with a disclaimer.

JZ UPSOUND: “ I am taking further legal advice on the prosecution of this appeal. I am concerned that this matter has occupied the public mind for some time now and deserves urgent attention.”

VO: Constitutional Law Expert Pierre de Vos is convinced the sudden change of heart, is fuelled by political motives rather than legal considerations.

PIERRE: In the law there is a provision that says you cannot appeal a judgement that you have already implemented//INT2 M14

VO: But it doesn’t stop anyone else from picking up the appeal and challenging the appointment of the commission.

LINK: While the commission of inquiry into State Capture may look like a win for civil society – the president still has a hand to play - the inquiry’s terms of reference will determine the scope of the investigation – and this is decided by the President.

PIERRE: Legally only the President can set the T of the commission of Inquiry – but the president now has some limitations on his power – if he wants to follow the PP report he must include all the matters investigated in the SC report – that doesn’t meant the pres cant add other aspects to his likening he can make the TOR as broad as he wants to make them INT2 M10

VO: Something the President has hinted at already.

RALPH: If you look in the ANC there is already a strong narrative that the big state capture is not with the Guptas – it’s with corporate SA. // And that is a leg that Pres JZ is standing on in his attempt to have a much wider investigation instead of focussing on his friends. INT2 M5

VO: ANC Veteran Mavuso Msimang agrees that corporate corruption must be investigated, but says this State Capture Inquiry is not the platform to address it.

MAVUSO: Lets not confuse what needs to be done immediately and urgently //any thing else will be seen as a digression. INT1 M10

VO: A matter, the then Public Protector responsible for the State of Capture Report – Thuli Madonsela, and her successor Busisiwe Mkhwebane – DON’t agree on.

Mkhwebane believes, the inquiry should NOT be limited to issues investigated or identified in the report. While Mandosela says, doing that would not ONLY be in defiance of the court order, but, it could also derail and delay the investigation.

Another important factor is who heads up the commission of inquiry. The task has fallen on Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo.

BEN: // it is somebody of stature – he has gone through the ranks, and he is not retired and that means he is somebody that can be trusted //. INT1 M2

VO: But De Vos believes it’s a task that comes with it’s own set of challenges - irrespective of who heads ups the inquiry.

PIERRE: HE is always at the service of the President // we know in past – both in SA and other countries – the person who appoints tries to keep some control by fiddling with the TOR to make sure that the right answer will come out of it. INT3 M16

VO: It’s a process OUTA will be watching closely as they are hopeful for serious outcomes.

BEN: First of all decisive action, recommendations, the number of people involved need to be identified and named and number three, they should be absolutely criminal case laid against these people so that they can go to jail INT1 M9

VO: But De Vos points out that a commission of inquiry is not an accountability mechanism, rather a fact finding one.

PIERRE: a commission of inquiry is not like a court of law – it cannot find anyone guilty or send anybody to jail – no matter what happens with the commission it’s not going to land anyone including the Gupta brothers in jail. INT3 M4 //

VO: And it will be at least 18 months to possibly 5 years before the process is finalised.

In the interim, it seems that President Zuma is still in the game.

LINK: The recalling of President JZ did not even make it onto the agenda at the NEC, but some say that is not necessarily a bad thing – it’s all about timing.

MAVUSO: // it will be risky and unwise for [Cyril Ramaphosa] to make a move when he wasn’t certain that everyone was behind him – failure would have been a disaster for the ANC // INT5 M2

VO: But both Msimang and policital analyst Mathekga agree that President Zuma’s days are numbered.

RALPH: It is the beginning of the end – even if he can push against his removal in the next few weeks or so, the best he can do is to negotiate a better exit package //. INT2 M7
VO: And it appears that’s exactly what the President is doing. The Mail & Gaurdian quoted ANC sources that claim the President Zuma’s exit plan is not without some tricky conditions… a claim the ANC denies.
It’s rumoured he is demanding that ANC MP Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma take over as the country’s interim president, if he steps down. The President, also wants some of his key Cabinet appointments, such as Energy Minister David Mahlobo and State Security Minister Bongani Bongo, to be retained.
BEN: // every day that man is in office is another day where havoc gets done to SA and the deeper we go into the quagmire the more difficult it becomes to come out. // INT2 M3 ////– we need to stop this rot today. INT1 M10


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: President Zuma appointed a commission of inquiry into State Capture – we ask, why now?

BEN: PResident Zuma is a strategist at heart // what we believe he has done is another chess move //INT2 M1

PROMO 2
VO: Will the State Capture Commission of Inquiry be clear cut, when President Zuma is the one to decides the term of reference determining the scope of investigation?

RALPH: And that // his attempt to have a much wider investigation instead of focussing on his friends. INT2 M5

PROMO 3
VO: President Zuma’s sudden implementation of the State Capture Inquiry seems to have delayed what some say is his imminent departure as the leader of South Africa.

RALPH: It is the beginning of the end – // the best he can do is to negotiate a better exit package //. INT2 M7
